title: The agent who ran out of float
instructions:
## You manage a mobile money agent network

An agent in a market town keeps turning customers away. Read her weekly figures and decide how the network, the float, and interoperability should work.

evidence.title: Agent ledger, one week
evidence.text:
Mon: cash-in 9,200, cash-out 2,100
Tue: cash-in 8,800, cash-out 1,900
Wed: cash-in 9,500, cash-out 2,400
Thu: cash-in 3,100 (turned customers away from 11:00), cash-out 1,800
Fri: cash-in 2,200 (turned customers away), cash-out 2,000
E-float on Monday morning: 30,000. Cash on hand on Monday morning: 5,000.

evidence.title: How agent float works
evidence.text: A cash-in moves e-float from the agent to the customer and cash from the customer to the agent. A cash-out does the reverse. The agent rebalances by depositing cash at a bank or super-agent to buy e-float, or withdrawing e-float as cash.

choices.text: She is running out of cash
choices.feedback: Cash-ins bring cash in; she has more cash each day, not less.

choices.text: She is running out of e-float: cash-ins far exceed cash-outs
choices.feedback: Correct. About 7,000 of e-float leaves each day and only 2,000 returns; by Thursday it is gone.
They came; she could not serve them.

nodes.title: Rebalancing
nodes.text: What should the agent do each day?

choices.text: Deposit the accumulated cash with a super-agent or bank to buy e-float before it runs out, ideally mid-morning
choices.feedback: Correct. Rebalancing is the agent's core daily task in a cash-in heavy location.
That turns away the business she is there for.

choices.text: Wait for cash-outs to restore the float
choices.feedback: Cash-outs are a fraction of cash-ins here; the float will not recover on its own.

nodes.title: Network design
nodes.text: The nearest bank is 40 km away. As the network manager, what helps most?

choices.text: A super-agent or roaming rebalancing service in the town, and a float credit line for high-volume agents
choices.feedback: Correct. Liquidity infrastructure close to agents is what makes rural networks work.

choices.text: More agents in the same market
choices.feedback: They would all face the same float problem.

nodes.title: Interoperability
nodes.text: A customer on another network wants to receive money from this agent's customers. Which arrangement makes that work?

choices.text: A central switch or bilateral links between providers that clear and settle transfers between wallets
choices.feedback: Correct. Interoperability needs a switch and settlement rules between providers, in Ghana through GhIPSS.

choices.text: The customer must open a wallet on every network
choices.feedback: That is the problem interoperability solves.
That moves cash, not e-money, and creates risk for the agent.

nodes.title: Measuring
nodes.text: Which metric tells you an agent is under-floated before customers complain?

choices.text: The share of hours per day with e-float below a threshold, from transaction and balance logs
choices.feedback: Correct. Float availability is an operational KPI you can compute from the system.
Experience does not show today's float.

choices.text: The number of customers in the town
choices.feedback: Demand matters, but availability is what you can act on.

nodes.title: Plan agreed
nodes.text: You arrange mid-morning rebalancing through a super-agent, a float line for the agent, and float-availability monitoring across the network.

hints: Follow the e-float: every cash-in spends it.
Rebalancing converts the cash pile back into e-float.
Interoperability is a switch plus settlement rules.

checks.label: You read the ledger and the float rules
At least four of the five decisions are right
checks.message: Fewer than four of the five were right. Read the feedback and run the case again.

realityNote: Agent liquidity is the most studied operational problem in mobile money; providers track float-outs per agent per day and route rebalancing vans and super-agents by that data.
